[1/3] Plan localStorage persistence for editor camera, view mode, projection, grid and snap

impact_assessment.why: The editor forgets its camera, view mode, projection and overlay settings on every reload, unlike Unity/Unreal workspaces.
impact_assessment.benefits: The browser console restores the editor camera and viewport toggles per game, with debounced saves and a safe fallback when storage is unavailable.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: browser localStorage; concurrency: debounced writes during camera drags; state: malformed stored JSON, game-name keys, game-view camera state, toggles restoring before the scene loads.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Snapshot only editor camera state, scope the key by game, validate/clamp restored values, save debounced on layout changes, restore after the first scene load, and catch storage errors.

[1/3] Plan a file-backed material library and editor assignment workflow

impact_assessment.why: Materials are core PBR assets, but the editor can only assign registry materials created in code; it cannot author, save or reuse material assets.
impact_assessment.benefits: save_material writes .kmaterial files and registers material.<name> for rendering, assign_material applies a saved material to a node with undo, and the console edits color/metallic/roughness/emissive fields.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 39 and two new actions; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: registry registration before scene loads, texture id resolution, undo assign, name safety, malformed files.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Register saved materials at session start before scene loading, resolve textures through the registry, validate through Material, save atomically, assign under history, and add library/assignment/reload regressions.

[1/3] Plan a draggable hierarchy tree with selection and drop-to-reparent

impact_assessment.why: The hierarchy is a flat multi-select list; reparenting needs a separate dropdown and button, unlike Unity/Unreal tree drag-and-drop.
impact_assessment.benefits: Tree rows show indentation and prefab badges, click/Ctrl-click selection keeps the existing set contract, and dropping a row onto another node or empty space reparents it through reparent_node.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: selection semantics, prefab groups, invalid/self/descendant drops, filtered rebuilds, drag cancellation.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Rebuild rows from the editor document, reuse select_many and reparent_node, mark drag-over rows, keep server validation authoritative, and add static tree/drag regressions.

[1/3] Plan material library delete/restore with in-use protection

impact_assessment.why: Saved materials can be created and assigned but never removed, so the material library grows without a lifecycle.
impact_assessment.benefits: delete_material moves unused materials to the recoverable trash and unregisters them; restore_material brings them back and re-registers material.<name> for rendering.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: editor schema 40 and two new actions; dependency: none; concurrency: editor lock; state: nodes still referencing deleted assets, registry removal, trash collisions, restore registration.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Block deletion while any current-scene node uses the material, move files through the shared trash helper, remove/register registry records, validate trash names, and add delete/restore/in-use regressions.

[1/3] Plan an animation timeline scrubber tied to clip duration and preview

impact_assessment.why: Animation preview only accepts a typed time; there is no visual timeline and no duration feedback.
impact_assessment.benefits: A range scrubber derives duration from a library clip or inline keys, mirrors the time field, and previews on release.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: UI-only, no API/schema change; dependency: none; concurrency: debounced preview actions; state: malformed clip JSON, zero-length clips, library duration, time clamping, scene refresh.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Parse key times defensively, prefer library duration, clamp both controls, preview only on change, and add static timeline wiring regressions.
